correctness.rationale: For squared error, the risk of the constant shift \(b\) is a strictly convex quadratic whose linear coefficient is \(E[X_{(2)}-\theta_{(2)}]\). This expectation reduces to the positive-part mean of a \(N(-\Delta,2)\) variable and gives the displayed closed form. Completing the square yields the exact regret identity. Direct differentiation gives \(h'(\Delta)=-\Phi(-\Delta/\sqrt2)\), proving strict monotonicity and uniqueness of the crossover. The packaged verifier independently checks the normal positive-part integral, derivative, root, and sign pattern.

value.rationale: The motivating paper makes the constant-shift class a central object, proves only an abstract pointwise-minimizer characterization there, and later uses simulation to describe the normal risk reversal. The finding supplies the missing closed oracle parameterization of the entire class, an exact regret identity, and the unique numerical phase boundary for the paper's boundary shift versus the usual estimator. Although the boundary shift is itself dominated by a nonconstant Brewster–Zidek rule, the result is a complete structural calculation for the source's natural class rather than an arbitrary slice.
